# Annual Leave and Carry-Forward Policy

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how paid annual leave is earned, requested, approved and carried forward at Meridian Technologies. It applies to all permanent employees in India, Singapore and the United Kingdom who are on payroll as of 1 January 2026. Contractors, interns and staff on fixed-term agreements shorter than six months are covered by their engagement letter instead and must not use the leave balances described here. ## 2. Entitlement

1. Full-time employees accrue 24 days of paid annual leave per calendar year.

3. Part-time employees accrue on a pro-rata basis using contracted hours divided by 40.
4. Employees on probation accrue leave from their first day but may not take more than five days until probation is confirmed.
5. Unused annual leave may be carried forward into the following calendar year up to a maximum of 12 days.
6. Carried-forward days must be used by 31 March of the year into which they were carried. Any balance remaining after 31 March is forfeited without payment in lieu.

Carry-forward is calculated by the payroll system on 31 December and appears on the January payslip. Employees who believe the figure is wrong must raise a ticket with People Operations within 30 days; corrections after that date require Finance approval because the provision has already been booked.

5. During a declared incident (Sev-1 or Sev-2), approved leave for on-call staff may be cancelled by the incident commander. Cancelled days are restored in full and are exempt from the carry-forward cap for that year.

# Parental Leave Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy sets out paid leave for birth, adoption and surrogacy for all permanent employees who have completed 90 days of continuous service. It applies equally to all genders; the entitlement depends on the caregiving role the employee declares, not on the employee's gender or the child's origin. Employees on fixed-term contracts of 12 months or more receive the same entitlement pro-rated to their remaining contract length.

## 2. Primary caregiver entitlement

1. A primary caregiver is entitled to 26 weeks of paid parental leave.
2. Leave may begin up to four weeks before the expected date of birth or the date of adoption placement.
3. Leave must be taken in a single continuous block. Splitting into two blocks is permitted only where the second block is taken within 12 months of the birth and the manager and People Operations both approve in writing.
4. Pay during primary caregiver leave is 100% of base salary for the first 26 weeks.
5. The employee returns to the same role and grade. If the role has been made redundant during the leave, the redundancy process must follow the Exit and Separation policy and the employee is entitled to redeployment priority for 90 days.

## 3. Secondary caregiver entitlement

1. A secondary caregiver is entitled to 6 weeks of paid parental leave.
2. Secondary leave may be taken in up to three blocks within 12 months of the birth or placement.
3. Pay during secondary caregiver leave is 100% of base salary.
4. A secondary caregiver may switch to primary caregiver status once, by written declaration, provided fewer than 13 weeks of the primary entitlement have been used. The switch requires People Operations approval and is recorded in the HR system.

# Subpoena and Litigation Hold

## 1. Immediate steps

1. Anyone who receives a subpoena, court order, regulatory request or formal notice of a dispute must notify Legal within 24 hours.
2. Do not respond to the requester, confirm receipt, or discuss the matter outside Legal.
3. Do not delete, edit or move any related record, including chat messages, emails and tickets.
4. Legal appoints a single point of contact for the matter.

## 2. Litigation hold

1. Legal issues a written hold to the custodians it identifies.
2. Custodians must acknowledge the hold within two business days.
3. The hold suspends every deletion rule in Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule, including automated purge jobs.
4. IT must suspend mailbox and backup deletion for the named custodians until Legal releases the hold.
5. Any loss of data after a hold is issued must be reported to Legal immediately.

## 3. Preservation scope

Preservation covers documents, emails, chat, tickets, code repositories, meeting recordings and device data. Legal defines the date range and custodian list; anything outside the range is not preserved but must not be destroyed if it may become relevant.

## 4. Collection and review

Collection is performed by IT at Legal's direction, with a documented chain of custody. Review is conducted by Legal and, where required, external counsel. Access to collected material is limited to the matter team.

## 5. Confidentiality

The existence of a subpoena is confidential and must not be discussed with customers, vendors or colleagues outside the matter team unless Legal approves. Breach of confidentiality can itself create legal exposure.

## 6. Release

Legal releases the hold in writing when the matter concludes. Normal retention resumes from the release date, and the retention clock is not shortened by the hold period.

# Subpoena and Litigation Hold

## 1. Immediate steps

1. Anyone who receives a subpoena, court order, regulatory request or formal notice of a dispute must notify Legal within 24 hours.
2. Do not respond to the requester, confirm receipt, or discuss the matter outside Legal.
3. Do not delete, edit or move any related record, including chat messages, emails and tickets.

1. Legal issues a written hold to the custodians it identifies.
2. Custodians must acknowledge the hold within two business days.
3. The hold suspends every deletion rule in Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule, including automated purge jobs.
4. IT must suspend mailbox and backup deletion for the named custodians until Legal releases the hold.
5. Any loss of data after a hold is issued must be reported to Legal immediately.

## 3. Preservation scope

## 4. Collection and review

Collection is performed by IT at Legal's direction, with a documented chain of custody. Review is conducted by Legal and, where required, external counsel. Access to collected material is limited to the matter team.

## 5. Confidentiality

The existence of a subpoena is confidential and must not be discussed with customers, vendors or colleagues outside the matter team unless Legal approves. Breach of confidentiality can itself create legal exposure.

## 6. Release

Legal releases the hold in writing when the matter concludes. Normal retention resumes from the release date, and the retention clock is not shortened by the hold period.

# Data Privacy and GDPR Compliance

## 1. Scope

This policy governs the processing of personal data of customers, employees, candidates and website visitors. It applies to every team and every system, including systems bought by a department without Legal involvement. Where local law is stricter than this policy, the stricter rule applies.

## 2. Lawful basis

Every processing activity needs a lawful basis recorded in the processing register: contract, legal obligation, legitimate interest, consent or vital interest. Marketing consent must be opt-in and separately recorded; pre-ticked boxes are not consent. Legitimate interest assessments are documented by the DPO.

## 3. Data subject rights

1. A data subject access request (DSAR) must be answered within 30 days of receipt.
2. The 30-day clock starts when the request reaches the privacy mailbox, not when the team begins work.
3. Identity must be verified before data is released; verification must not require excessive documentation.
4. Erasure requests are honoured unless a legal retention obligation applies under Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule.
5. Requests are logged, and the log is reviewed monthly by the DPO.

## 4. Breach notification

1. A suspected personal data breach must be reported to the DPO within 24 hours of discovery.
2. The DPO assesses whether the breach is notifiable; a notifiable breach is reported to the regulator within 72 hours.
3. Affected individuals are informed without undue delay where the breach is likely to result in high risk.
4. A breach log is maintained for five years.

## 5. Vendors and transfers

Vendors processing personal data require a Data Processing Agreement under IT_Vendor_Security_Review. Transfers outside the EEA require an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses. A transfer impact assessment is required for any new destination country.

## 6. Privacy by design

New systems and features must complete a data protection impact assessment before launch where they process sensitive data, profile individuals or use new technology. The DPIA is reviewed by the DPO and stored with the project record.

## 7. Training and audit

All employees complete privacy training annually. The DPO audits two teams per quarter against the processing register and reports findings to the audit committee.

## 8. Related documents

- IT_Data_Classification_Standard for data tiers.
- Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule for retention.
- IT_Vendor_Security_Review for vendor DPAs.

# Data Classification Standard

## 1. Purpose

Every piece of information Meridian holds has a classification. The classification determines who may access it, how it must be stored and shared, and how long it is kept. When in doubt, classify higher and ask the data owner; misclassifying downward is a security incident.

## 2. Tiers

| Tier | Definition | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Public | Approved for release outside the company | Marketing site copy, published pricing |
| Internal | Routine business information | Team documents, internal wiki, meeting notes |
| Confidential | Sensitive business or personal data | Customer contracts, employee records, financials |
| Restricted | Data whose loss causes severe harm | Payment credentials, health data, source code secrets |

2. **Internal** — company accounts only; may be shared with contractors under NDA.
3. **Confidential** — need-to-know; encrypted at rest and in transit; no sharing to personal email or personal cloud storage.
4. **Restricted** — named-individual access; encryption with company-managed keys; export requires the data owner's written approval; no copies on endpoints.

| Tier | Retention | Disposal |
|---|---|---|
| Public | 1 year after supersession | Delete |
| Internal | 3 years | Delete |
| Confidential | 5 years | Secure delete with certificate |

A purchase is capital expenditure when it costs more than INR 10,00,000 and provides benefit for more than 12 months. # Annual Leave and Carry-Forward Policy

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how paid annual leave is earned, requested, approved and carried forward at Meridian Technologies. It applies to all permanent employees in India, Singapore and the United Kingdom who are on payroll as of 1 January 2026. Contractors, interns and staff on fixed-term agreements shorter than six months are covered by their engagement letter instead and must not use the leave balances described here. Where a local statutory entitlement exceeds the entitlement in this policy, the statutory minimum applies and the difference is reported by People Operations in the quarterly compliance pack.

## 2. Entitlement

1. Full-time employees accrue 24 days of paid annual leave per calendar year.
2. Accrual is monthly and pro-rated from the date of joining. An employee joining on the 15th of a month accrues half of that month's entitlement.
3. Part-time employees accrue on a pro-rata basis using contracted hours divided by 40.
4. Employees on probation accrue leave from their first day but may not take more than five days until probation is confirmed.
5. Unused annual leave may be carried forward into the following calendar year up to a maximum of 12 days.
6. Carried-forward days must be used by 31 March of the year into which they were carried. Any balance remaining after 31 March is forfeited without payment in lieu.

Carry-forward is calculated by the payroll system on 31 December and appears on the January payslip. Employees who believe the figure is wrong must raise a ticket with People Operations within 30 days; corrections after that date require Finance approval because the provision has already been booked.

1. Leave must be requested in the HR system at least 10 working days before the first day of absence.
2. Requests of five consecutive days or more require approval from the employee's manager and from the department head.
3. Requests spanning a quarter end are automatically routed to the Finance business partner for the department.
4. Leave taken without approval is recorded as unpaid absence until regularised, and regularisation must happen within five working days of return.
5. During a declared incident (Sev-1 or Sev-2), approved leave for on-call staff may be cancelled by the incident commander. Cancelled days are restored in full and are exempt from the carry-forward cap for that year.

# Return to Office Mandate

## 1. Background

Meridian moved to a hybrid model in 2022. Between 2022 and 2025 the expectation was set locally by each department, which produced inconsistent attendance and made desk planning unreliable. This mandate replaces departmental guidance with a single company-wide minimum. It supersedes all previous versions in full; where a team charter conflicts with this document, this document governs.

## 2. Minimum attendance

1. Effective 1 July 2026, all employees must be on-site a minimum of 4 days per week.
2. The remaining day may be worked remotely, subject to HR_Remote_Work_Policy.
3. Employees whose role is designated on-site-only must attend 5 days per week.
4. Attendance is measured by badge-in events, not by calendar blocks. Two badge-ins on the same day count as one day.
5. A week containing a public holiday is pro-rated: three on-site days are required in a four-day week.

## 3. Anchor days

Tuesday and Thursday are company anchor days. Every team must have at least 80% attendance on anchor days. Team offsites, customer visits and approved travel count as attendance. Anchor days may be moved for a whole team by the department head with two weeks' notice, but not more than twice per quarter.

## 4. Transition and previous version

Version 2.1 of this mandate, effective 1 September 2025, required 3 days per week. That requirement remains in force until 30 June 2026. Employees and managers planning beyond that date must plan against the 4-day requirement in Section 2. People Operations will not grant individual exceptions to the 4-day minimum; the only permitted variations are statutory accommodation, approved medical accommodation, and the phased return described in HR_Parental_Leave.

## 5. Desk and space allocation

Desks are not assigned. Teams receive a neighbourhood and book desks through the facilities system. Bookings open 14 days ahead and expire at 10:30 on the booked day if not checked in. Meeting rooms are booked separately. Employees who attend fewer than the required days release their desk booking priority to colleagues who attend more.

## 6. Compliance

2. A first month below the minimum triggers a conversation with the manager.

## 1. Severity definitions

1. **Sev-1** — customer-facing outage or data loss affecting more than 20% of customers, or any confirmed security breach.
2. **Sev-2** — degraded service affecting a material subset of customers, or an internal system blocking a revenue process.
3. **Sev-3** — limited impact with a workaround.
4. **Sev-4** — cosmetic or single-user issue.

Severity is declared by the on-call engineer and may be raised by the incident commander at any time. Downgrading a Sev-1 requires the incident commander and the engineering director.

## 2. Response windows

|---|---|---|

The incident commander owns the incident and does not debug. The communications lead writes status updates. The subject-matter engineers investigate. The scribe keeps the timeline. For a Sev-1, the incident commander is the on-call engineering manager; for a Sev-2 it may be the on-call engineer.

# Change Management Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy controls how changes reach production so that reliability is not traded for speed. It applies to application deploys, infrastructure changes, database migrations, configuration changes and third-party integrations. Documentation-only changes and changes made entirely inside a feature-flagged path that is off in production are exempt.

## 2. Change types

1. **Standard** — pre-approved, low-risk changes with a documented runbook, such as a routine dependency patch or a dashboard update.
2. **Normal** — any change that is not standard or emergency; requires review and a change record.

Every normal change must have a tested rollback plan. Database migrations must be backward compatible for at least one release so the application can roll back without restoring data. A change without a rollback plan is rejected by the CAB.

2. If the change is implicated in an incident, roll back first and investigate afterwards.

# Vendor Security Review

## 1. When a review is required

Any third party that will store, process or access Meridian data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. This includes SaaS tools, contractors with system access, managed services and data processors. A review is not required for vendors that receive only Public information, but the classification must be recorded.

## 2. Process and timelines

1. The business owner submits the vendor request with the intended data classification and integration scope.
2. Security Engineering sends the standard questionnaire within 2 working days.
3. The vendor returns the questionnaire and evidence. The review concludes within 30 days of receiving complete evidence.
4. Reviews requiring a penetration test summary or a Data Processing Agreement take up to 45 days.
5. Contracts must not be signed before the review is recorded as passed.

## 3. Evidence requirements

1. SOC 2 Type II is required for any vendor processing Confidential or Restricted data. A SOC 2 Type I is accepted only with a remediation plan and a follow-up date.
2. ISO 27001 certification is accepted in place of SOC 2 where the scope covers the service in question.
3. Vendors without either certification require a documented compensating review by Security Engineering and approval from the CTO.
4. Encryption at rest and in transit must be evidenced.
5. Sub-processors must be listed and approved; unreported sub-processors are a contractual breach.

## 4. Data processing terms

Where personal data is involved, Legal_Data_Privacy_GDPR_Compliance requires a Data Processing Agreement. The DPA must cover purpose limitation, breach notification within 72 hours, deletion on termination and audit rights. Vendors that cannot accept the standard terms are escalated to Legal.

## 5. Ongoing monitoring

1. Confidential and Restricted vendors are reassessed annually.
2. A vendor security incident must be reported to Meridian within 72 hours under the DPA.
3. Access granted to vendor staff is reviewed quarterly with the vendor's named contacts.
4. Vendors that fail two consecutive reassessments are placed on a remediation plan and may be terminated by the business owner.

## 6. Exceptions

An exception requires the CTO's written approval, a compensating control and an expiry date no later than 90 days. Exceptions are reported to the security committee monthly.

# Subpoena and Litigation Hold

## 1. Immediate steps

1. Anyone who receives a subpoena, court order, regulatory request or formal notice of a dispute must notify Legal within 24 hours.
2. Do not respond to the requester, confirm receipt, or discuss the matter outside Legal.
3. Do not delete, edit or move any related record, including chat messages, emails and tickets.
4. Legal appoints a single point of contact for the matter.

## 2. Litigation hold

1. Legal issues a written hold to the custodians it identifies.
2. Custodians must acknowledge the hold within two business days.
3. The hold suspends every deletion rule in Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule, including automated purge jobs.
4. IT must suspend mailbox and backup deletion for the named custodians until Legal releases the hold.
5. Any loss of data after a hold is issued must be reported to Legal immediately.

## 3. Preservation scope

Preservation covers documents, emails, chat, tickets, code repositories, meeting recordings and device data. Legal defines the date range and custodian list; anything outside the range is not preserved but must not be destroyed if it may become relevant.

## 4. Collection and review

Collection is performed by IT at Legal's direction, with a documented chain of custody. Review is conducted by Legal and, where required, external counsel. Access to collected material is limited to the matter team.

## 5. Confidentiality

The existence of a subpoena is confidential and must not be discussed with customers, vendors or colleagues outside the matter team unless Legal approves. Breach of confidentiality can itself create legal exposure.

## 6. Release

Legal releases the hold in writing when the matter concludes. Normal retention resumes from the release date, and the retention clock is not shortened by the hold period.

# Data Privacy and GDPR Compliance

## 1. Scope

This policy governs the processing of personal data of customers, employees, candidates and website visitors. It applies to every team and every system, including systems bought by a department without Legal involvement. Where local law is stricter than this policy, the stricter rule applies.

## 2. Lawful basis

Every processing activity needs a lawful basis recorded in the processing register: contract, legal obligation, legitimate interest, consent or vital interest. Marketing consent must be opt-in and separately recorded; pre-ticked boxes are not consent. Legitimate interest assessments are documented by the DPO.

## 3. Data subject rights

1. A data subject access request (DSAR) must be answered within 30 days of receipt.
2. The 30-day clock starts when the request reaches the privacy mailbox, not when the team begins work.
3. Identity must be verified before data is released; verification must not require excessive documentation.
4. Erasure requests are honoured unless a legal retention obligation applies under Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule.
5. Requests are logged, and the log is reviewed monthly by the DPO.

## 4. Breach notification

1. A suspected personal data breach must be reported to the DPO within 24 hours of discovery.
2. The DPO assesses whether the breach is notifiable; a notifiable breach is reported to the regulator within 72 hours.
3. Affected individuals are informed without undue delay where the breach is likely to result in high risk.
4. A breach log is maintained for five years.

## 5. Vendors and transfers

Vendors processing personal data require a Data Processing Agreement under IT_Vendor_Security_Review. Transfers outside the EEA require an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses. A transfer impact assessment is required for any new destination country.

## 6. Privacy by design

New systems and features must complete a data protection impact assessment before launch where they process sensitive data, profile individuals or use new technology. The DPIA is reviewed by the DPO and stored with the project record.

## 7. Training and audit

# Records Retention Schedule

## 1. Purpose

This schedule states how long each category of record is kept and when the retention clock starts. Keeping records longer than necessary creates privacy and discovery risk; deleting them early breaches legal obligations. Where two rules conflict, the longer period applies.

## 2. Schedule

|---|---|---|
| Executed contracts | 8 years | Contract expiry or termination |
| Contract drafts and redlines | 3 years | Contract signature |

| Recruitment records | 1 year | Application date |

# Revenue Recognition Policy

## 1. Principle

Revenue is recognised when control of the promised service passes to the customer, in the amount the company expects to be entitled to. Meridian applies the five-step model: identify the contract, identify the performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate the price to the obligations, and recognise revenue as each obligation is satisfied.

## 2. Contract identification

A contract exists when it is approved, the rights and payment terms are identifiable, it has commercial substance, and collection is probable. Orders below INR 1,00,000 with a standard online acceptance are treated as contracts on acceptance. Deals with non-standard terms require Legal_Contract_Review_Process before revenue can be scheduled.

## 3. Performance obligations

1. Subscription access is a series of distinct daily services recognised over the contract term.
2. Implementation services are a separate obligation when the customer can benefit from them independently; otherwise they are combined with the subscription.
3. Training is a separate obligation recognised when delivered.
4. Hardware resold with software is recognised on delivery.

## 4. Transaction price

1. The transaction price includes fixed fees and variable consideration that is probable and estimable.
2. Discounts are allocated proportionally across obligations unless the contract evidences a standalone price for one obligation.
3. Rebates and service credits are estimated and constrained until the uncertainty resolves.
4. Significant financing components are adjusted where payment terms exceed 12 months.

## 5. Milestone and deferred revenue

1. Annual prepayments are recorded as deferred revenue and released monthly over the term.
2. Milestone billing on implementation is recognised against delivery of the milestone, not against the invoice date.
3. Where a milestone is invoiced before delivery, the balance sits in deferred revenue.
4. Where delivery precedes invoicing, an unbilled receivable is recorded.

## 6. Contract modifications

A modification is treated as a separate contract if it adds distinct services priced at standalone selling price. Otherwise the remaining consideration is reallocated over the remaining obligations. Modifications must be documented by the deal desk and approved by the Controller.

# Vendor Payment Terms

## 1. Default terms

1. The default payment term for vendor invoices is Net 45 from the invoice date.
2. The invoice date is the date the invoice is issued, not the date it is received.
3. Payment runs happen twice a month, on the 10th and the 25th. An invoice falling due between runs is paid on the next run.
4. Vendors must quote a purchase order number on every invoice; invoices without one are returned unpaid.

## 2. Early payment discount

1. Where a vendor offers a 2% discount for payment within 10 days, Accounts Payable takes the discount if the cash position allows.
2. The discount is calculated on the invoice value excluding taxes.
3. Discounts are recorded as a separate line in the vendor ledger, not netted against the payable.
4. Vendors offering a discount for payment within 5 days are reviewed by the treasury team before acceptance.

## 3. Invoice validation

1. A three-way match is required: purchase order, goods receipt and invoice.
2. Mismatches are resolved with the business owner within 5 working days.
3. Invoices above INR 10,00,000 require a second Finance review.
4. Duplicate invoices are flagged by the vendor ledger and are never paid twice.

## 4. Late payment

1. Interest is payable on late invoices at 1% per month where the delay exceeds 30 days beyond the agreed term.
2. Interest is not payable where the delay is caused by a missing purchase order or a disputed invoice.
3. Persistent late payment is reported to the CFO monthly.

## 5. Small invoices

Invoices below INR 5,00,000 are settled on Net 30 rather than Net 45. This exception exists to reduce the administrative cost of low-value payables and does not require a contract amendment. Where a contract states Net 45 for a vendor whose invoices are consistently below the threshold, Accounts Payable applies Net 30 and records the deviation in the vendor file. Business owners should expect the shorter term when planning cash.

## 6. Foreign currency

Foreign currency invoices are paid in the invoice currency. The exchange rate is the bank rate on the payment date. Vendors may not require payment in a currency other than the contract currency.

# Incident Response Runbook

## 1. Severity definitions

1. **Sev-1** — customer-facing outage or data loss affecting more than 20% of customers, or any confirmed security breach.
2. **Sev-2** — degraded service affecting a material subset of customers, or an internal system blocking a revenue process.
3. **Sev-3** — limited impact with a workaround.
4. **Sev-4** — cosmetic or single-user issue.

Severity is declared by the on-call engineer and may be raised by the incident commander at any time. Downgrading a Sev-1 requires the incident commander and the engineering director.

## 2. Response windows

| Step | Sev-1 | Sev-2 |
|---|---|---|
| Acknowledge page | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Open incident channel | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Status page update | 30 minutes | 2 hours |
| Customer communication | 1 hour | 4 hours |

Missing an acknowledgement window is tracked as a reliability metric, not a disciplinary matter, unless it is repeated.

## 3. Roles

The incident commander owns the incident and does not debug. The communications lead writes status updates. The subject-matter engineers investigate. The scribe keeps the timeline. For a Sev-1, the incident commander is the on-call engineering manager; for a Sev-2 it may be the on-call engineer.

3. Assign the four roles.
4. Mitigate first, diagnose second. Roll back if the change is the suspected cause.
5. Update the status page at the intervals in Section 2.

## 1. Scope

This policy covers resignation, termination, redundancy and retirement for all permanent employees. It does not cover contractors, whose notice terms are in their engagement letter.

## 2. Notice periods

1. Employees at L4 and above serve 60 days' notice.
2. Employees at L1 to L3 serve 30 days' notice.
3. Employees in their first 90 days serve 15 days' notice.

5. Meridian may pay salary in lieu of notice, in whole or in part, at its discretion.

# Parental Leave Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy sets out paid leave for birth, adoption and surrogacy for all permanent employees who have completed 90 days of continuous service. It applies equally to all genders; the entitlement depends on the caregiving role the employee declares, not on the employee's gender or the child's origin. Employees on fixed-term contracts of 12 months or more receive the same entitlement pro-rated to their remaining contract length.

## 2. Primary caregiver entitlement

1. A primary caregiver is entitled to 26 weeks of paid parental leave.
2. Leave may begin up to four weeks before the expected date of birth or the date of adoption placement.
3. Leave must be taken in a single continuous block. Splitting into two blocks is permitted only where the second block is taken within 12 months of the birth and the manager and People Operations both approve in writing.
4. Pay during primary caregiver leave is 100% of base salary for the first 26 weeks.
5. The employee returns to the same role and grade. If the role has been made redundant during the leave, the redundancy process must follow the Exit and Separation policy and the employee is entitled to redeployment priority for 90 days.

## 3. Secondary caregiver entitlement

1. A secondary caregiver is entitled to 6 weeks of paid parental leave.
2. Secondary leave may be taken in up to three blocks within 12 months of the birth or placement.
3. Pay during secondary caregiver leave is 100% of base salary.
4. A secondary caregiver may switch to primary caregiver status once, by written declaration, provided fewer than 13 weeks of the primary entitlement have been used. The switch requires People Operations approval and is recorded in the HR system.

## 4. Adoption and surrogacy

1. Adoption is treated identically to birth for both entitlements.
2. Leave may begin on the date the child is placed with the employee, not the date the adoption is legally finalised.
3. Employees pursuing surrogacy are entitled to the secondary caregiver entitlement, and to the primary entitlement where they are the sole intended parent.
4. Documentation required: placement letter from the adoption agency or a surrogacy agreement summary. Medical details are never required.

# Annual Leave and Carry-Forward Policy

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how paid annual leave is earned, requested, approved and carried forward at Meridian Technologies. It applies to all permanent employees in India, Singapore and the United Kingdom who are on payroll as of 1 January 2026. Contractors, interns and staff on fixed-term agreements shorter than six months are covered by their engagement letter instead and must not use the leave balances described here. Where a local statutory entitlement exceeds the entitlement in this policy, the statutory minimum applies and the difference is reported by People Operations in the quarterly compliance pack.

## 2. Entitlement

1. Full-time employees accrue 24 days of paid annual leave per calendar year.
2. Accrual is monthly and pro-rated from the date of joining. An employee joining on the 15th of a month accrues half of that month's entitlement.
3. Part-time employees accrue on a pro-rata basis using contracted hours divided by 40.
4. Employees on probation accrue leave from their first day but may not take more than five days until probation is confirmed.
5. Unused annual leave may be carried forward into the following calendar year up to a maximum of 12 days.
6. Carried-forward days must be used by 31 March of the year into which they were carried. Any balance remaining after 31 March is forfeited without payment in lieu.

Carry-forward is calculated by the payroll system on 31 December and appears on the January payslip. Employees who believe the figure is wrong must raise a ticket with People Operations within 30 days; corrections after that date require Finance approval because the provision has already been booked.

1. Leave must be requested in the HR system at least 10 working days before the first day of absence.
2. Requests of five consecutive days or more require approval from the employee's manager and from the department head.

4. Leave taken without approval is recorded as unpaid absence until regularised, and regularisation must happen within five working days of return.
5. During a declared incident (Sev-1 or Sev-2), approved leave for on-call staff may be cancelled by the incident commander. Cancelled days are restored in full and are exempt from the carry-forward cap for that year.

# Capital Expenditure Policy

## 1. Definition

A purchase is capital expenditure when it costs more than INR 10,00,000 and provides benefit for more than 12 months. Below that threshold the purchase is expensed in the quarter it is incurred, even if it is hardware. Software subscriptions are expensed unless the contract grants a perpetual licence, in which case the licence fee is capitalised and the support element is expensed.

## 2. Approval

1. Capex requires a business case covering the problem, the options considered, the total cost of ownership, the payback period and the risk of not proceeding.
2. A payback period longer than 24 months requires the CFO's approval; longer than 36 months requires board approval.
3. Every capex request must name the budget line in Finance_Quarterly_Budget_Allocation.
4. Capex above INR 50,00,000 is reviewed by the investment committee, which meets monthly.

## 3. Capitalisation and depreciation

| Asset class | Useful life | Method |
|---|---|---|
| Computer hardware | 3 years | Straight line |
| Network equipment | 5 years | Straight line |
| Furniture and fixtures | 7 years | Straight line |
| Perpetual software licences | 3 years | Straight line |
| Leasehold improvements | Shorter of lease or 5 years | Straight line |

Depreciation starts in the month the asset is available for use, not the month it is paid for. Assets not yet in use are held as capital work in progress and reviewed each quarter.

## 4. Impairment

Assets are reviewed for impairment annually or when there is an indicator such as a product being discontinued. An impairment loss is recognised in the quarter it is identified and reported to the CFO.

## 5. Disposal

1. Disposal requires the asset owner's request and Finance approval.
2. Proceeds are recorded against the asset's net book value; any gain or loss is recognised in the income statement.
3. Data-bearing assets must be wiped under IT_Data_Classification_Standard before disposal, with a certificate retained.
4. Disposals above INR 5,00,000 are reported to the audit committee.

## 6. Leases

Leases longer than 12 months are recognised on the balance sheet in line with the applicable accounting standard. The facilities team maintains the lease register and provides it to Finance quarterly.

No. Corporate travel cover applies automatically to every business trip booked through the corporate travel tool. Buying separate cover is not reimbursable.

Medical treatment and evacuation up to USD 250,000, trip cancellation, baggage loss up to USD 1,500, and personal liability. Pre-existing conditions are covered for business travel only.

## 3. How do I claim?

Call the insurer's assistance line before any treatment. Keep every receipt and submit the claim within 30 days of returning. Finance can provide the policy number and the assistance card.

## 4. Leisure add-ons

Extending a trip for leisure is allowed with manager approval, but the leisure portion is not covered and any change fee is personal.

# Quarterly Budget Allocation

## 1. Cycle

Meridian plans in financial quarters ending June, September, December and March. The annual plan is approved by the board in March and split into quarterly envelopes. Department heads receive their envelope in the first week of the quarter and may commit spend against it from day one.

## 2. FY2026 Q3 envelopes

| Department | Envelope (INR lakh) | Headcount | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engineering | 420 | 180 | Includes cloud and tooling |
| Sales | 310 | 65 | Excludes commissions |
| Marketing | 145 | 22 | Events capped at 40% |
| Operations | 120 | 40 | Facilities and support |
| HR | 85 | 18 | Includes L&D central fund |
| Legal | 40 | 9 | External counsel capped at 25% |
| Finance | 55 | 21 | Audit fees included |

## 3. Reallocation

1. Up to 10% of an envelope may be reallocated between lines within the same department without approval.
2. Reallocation above 10% requires the CFO's approval and must be requested within 10 working days of the quarter start.
3. Reallocation between departments is not permitted after the quarter's second month.
4. Unspent envelope does not carry into the next quarter except for committed purchase orders.

## 4. Contingency

A 10% contingency is held centrally and released by the CFO. Requests for contingency must state the business impact of not funding and the offsetting saving elsewhere. Contingency requests are decided weekly on Thursdays.

1. A commitment exists when a purchase order is issued.
2. Finance accrues for services received but not invoiced at quarter end.
3. Department heads review their accrual report in the first three working days of the new quarter.
4. Late invoices against a closed quarter are charged to the current quarter unless the accrual was recorded.

## 6. Headcount

Headcount changes require the CFO and the Chief People Officer to sign off. Backfills are approved by the department head within the approved envelope. New roles in Q3 are frozen unless funded by contingency.

# Vendor Security Review

## 1. When a review is required

Any third party that will store, process or access Meridian data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. This includes SaaS tools, contractors with system access, managed services and data processors. A review is not required for vendors that receive only Public information, but the classification must be recorded.

## 2. Process and timelines

1. The business owner submits the vendor request with the intended data classification and integration scope.

3. The vendor returns the questionnaire and evidence. The review concludes within 30 days of receiving complete evidence.

1. SOC 2 Type II is required for any vendor processing Confidential or Restricted data. A SOC 2 Type I is accepted only with a remediation plan and a follow-up date.

4. Vendors that fail two consecutive reassessments are placed on a remediation plan and may be terminated by the business owner.

An exception requires the CTO's written approval, a compensating control and an expiry date no later than 90 days. Exceptions are reported to the security committee monthly.

# Incident Response Runbook

## 1. Severity definitions

1. **Sev-1** — customer-facing outage or data loss affecting more than 20% of customers, or any confirmed security breach.
2. **Sev-2** — degraded service affecting a material subset of customers, or an internal system blocking a revenue process.
3. **Sev-3** — limited impact with a workaround.
4. **Sev-4** — cosmetic or single-user issue.

Severity is declared by the on-call engineer and may be raised by the incident commander at any time. Downgrading a Sev-1 requires the incident commander and the engineering director.

## 2. Response windows

| Step | Sev-1 | Sev-2 |
|---|---|---|
| Acknowledge page | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Open incident channel | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Status page update | 30 minutes | 2 hours |
| Customer communication | 1 hour | 4 hours |

Missing an acknowledgement window is tracked as a reliability metric, not a disciplinary matter, unless it is repeated.

## 3. Roles

The incident commander owns the incident and does not debug. The communications lead writes status updates. The subject-matter engineers investigate. The scribe keeps the timeline. For a Sev-1, the incident commander is the on-call engineering manager; for a Sev-2 it may be the on-call engineer.

## 4. Process

1. Acknowledge the page and declare severity in the incident channel.
2. Open the bridge. For a Sev-1, the bridge must open within 15 minutes of declaration; see Operations_Sev_Incident_Escalation for the current runbook version.
3. Assign the four roles.
4. Mitigate first, diagnose second. Roll back if the change is the suspected cause.
5. Update the status page at the intervals in Section 2.
6. Resolve only when the customer impact has ended, not when the root cause is understood.

## 5. Communication

Internal updates go in the incident channel every 30 minutes for a Sev-1 and every 2 hours for a Sev-2. Customer updates are written by the communications lead and approved by the incident commander. Never speculate about root cause in a customer update.

## 6. Postmortem

1. A postmortem is required for every Sev-1 and Sev-2.

# Incident Response Runbook

## 1. Severity definitions

1. **Sev-1** — customer-facing outage or data loss affecting more than 20% of customers, or any confirmed security breach.
2. **Sev-2** — degraded service affecting a material subset of customers, or an internal system blocking a revenue process.
3. **Sev-3** — limited impact with a workaround.
4. **Sev-4** — cosmetic or single-user issue.

Severity is declared by the on-call engineer and may be raised by the incident commander at any time. Downgrading a Sev-1 requires the incident commander and the engineering director.

## 2. Response windows

| Step | Sev-1 | Sev-2 |
|---|---|---|
| Acknowledge page | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Open incident channel | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Status page update | 30 minutes | 2 hours |
| Customer communication | 1 hour | 4 hours |

Missing an acknowledgement window is tracked as a reliability metric, not a disciplinary matter, unless it is repeated.

## 3. Roles

The incident commander owns the incident and does not debug. The communications lead writes status updates. The subject-matter engineers investigate. The scribe keeps the timeline. For a Sev-1, the incident commander is the on-call engineering manager; for a Sev-2 it may be the on-call engineer.

Internal updates go in the incident channel every 30 minutes for a Sev-1 and every 2 hours for a Sev-2. Customer updates are written by the communications lead and approved by the incident commander. Never speculate about root cause in a customer update.

## 6. Postmortem

1. A postmortem is required for every Sev-1 and Sev-2.

# Access Control Standard

## 1. Scope

This standard defines how identities are created, authenticated, authorised and removed across Meridian systems. It applies to employees, contractors, service accounts and third-party integrations. Where a system cannot meet this standard, the exception is documented and approved by the security team with a remediation date.

## 2. Authentication

1. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for every system that holds Internal, Confidential or Restricted data.
2. Passwords must be at least 14 characters and are checked against a breach corpus at set time.
3. Shared accounts are prohibited. Service accounts must be owned by a named team and rotated every 90 days.
4. Session lifetime is 12 hours for web applications and 8 hours for administrative consoles.
5. SSH access requires a hardware key or a short-lived certificate; password authentication is disabled.

## 3. Authorisation

1. Access follows least privilege: the minimum needed to do the job, granted per role.
2. Role definitions are owned by the system owner and reviewed quarterly.
3. Privileged access — production write, cloud administration, payment systems — is granted for a maximum of 90 days and requires a second approver.
4. Access to customer data requires the data owner's approval and is logged.
5. A manager's approval is required for any new role assignment and is recorded in the access system.

## 4. Reviews

1. Every quarter, managers review the access of their direct reports and confirm or revoke.
2. Reviews are due within 10 working days of the request; overdue reviews escalate to the department head.
3. Dormant accounts with no login for 60 days are disabled automatically.
4. Contractor accounts expire on the engagement end date without exception.

Joining access is provisioned from the HR record on day one (see HR_Employee_Onboarding_Guide). A role change triggers a re-review of all access within five working days. # Vendor Security Review

## 1. When a review is required

Any third party that will store, process or access Meridian data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. This includes SaaS tools, contractors with system access, managed services and data processors. A review is not required for vendors that receive only Public information, but the classification must be recorded.

## 2. Process and timelines

1. The business owner submits the vendor request with the intended data classification and integration scope.
2. Security Engineering sends the standard questionnaire within 2 working days.
3. The vendor returns the questionnaire and evidence. The review concludes within 30 days of receiving complete evidence.
4. Reviews requiring a penetration test summary or a Data Processing Agreement take up to 45 days.
5. Contracts must not be signed before the review is recorded as passed.

## 3. Evidence requirements

1. SOC 2 Type II is required for any vendor processing Confidential or Restricted data. A SOC 2 Type I is accepted only with a remediation plan and a follow-up date.
2. ISO 27001 certification is accepted in place of SOC 2 where the scope covers the service in question.
3. Vendors without either certification require a documented compensating review by Security Engineering and approval from the CTO.
4. Encryption at rest and in transit must be evidenced.
5. Sub-processors must be listed and approved; unreported sub-processors are a contractual breach.

## 4. Data processing terms

Where personal data is involved, Legal_Data_Privacy_GDPR_Compliance requires a Data Processing Agreement. The DPA must cover purpose limitation, breach notification within 72 hours, deletion on termination and audit rights. Vendors that cannot accept the standard terms are escalated to Legal.

## 5. Ongoing monitoring

1. Confidential and Restricted vendors are reassessed annually.
2. A vendor security incident must be reported to Meridian within 72 hours under the DPA.
3. Access granted to vendor staff is reviewed quarterly with the vendor's named contacts.
4. Vendors that fail two consecutive reassessments are placed on a remediation plan and may be terminated by the business owner.

## 6. Exceptions

An exception requires the CTO's written approval, a compensating control and an expiry date no later than 90 days. Exceptions are reported to the security committee monthly.

- IT_Access_Control_Standard for vendor accounts.
- Legal_Contract_Review_Process

# Change Management Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy controls how changes reach production so that reliability is not traded for speed. It applies to application deploys, infrastructure changes, database migrations, configuration changes and third-party integrations. Documentation-only changes and changes made entirely inside a feature-flagged path that is off in production are exempt.

1. **Standard** — pre-approved, low-risk changes with a documented runbook, such as a routine dependency patch or a dashboard update.
2. **Normal** — any change that is not standard or emergency; requires review and a change record.

1. Open a change record describing the change, the systems affected, the rollback plan and the monitoring plan.

2. If the change is implicated in an incident, roll back first and investigate afterwards.

Rooms are booked through the calendar system. Bookings open 14 days ahead and are limited to 4 hours per booking. Recurring bookings are limited to 8 weeks and must be re-confirmed afterwards.

# Incident Response Runbook

## 1. Severity definitions

1. **Sev-1** — customer-facing outage or data loss affecting more than 20% of customers, or any confirmed security breach.
2. **Sev-2** — degraded service affecting a material subset of customers, or an internal system blocking a revenue process.
3. **Sev-3** — limited impact with a workaround.
4. **Sev-4** — cosmetic or single-user issue.

Severity is declared by the on-call engineer and may be raised by the incident commander at any time. Downgrading a Sev-1 requires the incident commander and the engineering director.

## 2. Response windows

| Step | Sev-1 | Sev-2 |
|---|---|---|
| Acknowledge page | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Open incident channel | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Status page update | 30 minutes | 2 hours |
| Customer communication | 1 hour | 4 hours |

Missing an acknowledgement window is tracked as a reliability metric, not a disciplinary matter, unless it is repeated.

## 3. Roles

The incident commander owns the incident and does not debug. The communications lead writes status updates. The subject-matter engineers investigate. The scribe keeps the timeline. For a Sev-1, the incident commander is the on-call engineering manager; for a Sev-2 it may be the on-call engineer.

## 4. Process

1. Acknowledge the page and declare severity in the incident channel.
2. Open the bridge. For a Sev-1, the bridge must open within 15 minutes of declaration; see Operations_Sev_Incident_Escalation for the current runbook version.
3. Assign the four roles.
4. Mitigate first, diagnose second. Roll back if the change is the suspected cause.
5. Update the status page at the intervals in Section 2.
6. Resolve only when the customer impact has ended, not when the root cause is understood.

## 5. Communication

Internal updates go in the incident channel every 30 minutes for a Sev-1 and every 2 hours for a Sev-2. Customer updates are written by the communications lead and approved by the incident commander. Never speculate about root cause in a customer update.

## 6. Postmortem

1. A postmortem is required for every Sev-1 and Sev-2.

# Change Management Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy controls how changes reach production so that reliability is not traded for speed. It applies to application deploys, infrastructure changes, database migrations, configuration changes and third-party integrations. Documentation-only changes and changes made entirely inside a feature-flagged path that is off in production are exempt.

## 2. Change types

1. **Standard** — pre-approved, low-risk changes with a documented runbook, such as a routine dependency patch or a dashboard update.
2. **Normal** — any change that is not standard or emergency; requires review and a change record.
3. **Emergency** — a change needed to resolve an active Sev-1 or Sev-2. Emergency changes may proceed with verbal approval from the incident commander and are recorded retrospectively within one business day.

## 3. Normal change process

1. Open a change record describing the change, the systems affected, the rollback plan and the monitoring plan.
2. Obtain code review from at least one engineer who is not the author.
3. Obtain approval from the system owner. Changes touching payment flows also require Finance sign-off.
4. Submit to the Change Advisory Board (CAB) at least 5 business days before the planned deployment window.
5. Deploy in the approved window and watch the dashboards for 30 minutes.
6. Close the change record with the observed outcome.

The CAB meets every Tuesday at 15:00 IST. Changes submitted after the Monday 12:00 cut-off are considered the following week. A change rejected by the CAB may be re-submitted once with the requested amendments.

## 4. Deployment windows

Production deploys are permitted Monday to Thursday, 10:00 to 17:00 IST. Friday deploys require the engineering director's approval. Every normal change must have a tested rollback plan. Database migrations must be backward compatible for at least one release so the application can roll back without restoring data. A change without a rollback plan is rejected by the CAB.

2. If the change is implicated in an incident, roll back first and investigate afterwards.

# Vendor Security Review

## 1. When a review is required

Any third party that will store, process or access Meridian data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. This includes SaaS tools, contractors with system access, managed services and data processors. A review is not required for vendors that receive only Public information, but the classification must be recorded.

## 2. Process and timelines

1. The business owner submits the vendor request with the intended data classification and integration scope.
2. Security Engineering sends the standard questionnaire within 2 working days.
3. The vendor returns the questionnaire and evidence. The review concludes within 30 days of receiving complete evidence.
4. Reviews requiring a penetration test summary or a Data Processing Agreement take up to 45 days.
5. Contracts must not be signed before the review is recorded as passed.

## 3. Evidence requirements

1. SOC 2 Type II is required for any vendor processing Confidential or Restricted data. A SOC 2 Type I is accepted only with a remediation plan and a follow-up date.
2. ISO 27001 certification is accepted in place of SOC 2 where the scope covers the service in question.
3. Vendors without either certification require a documented compensating review by Security Engineering and approval from the CTO.
4. Encryption at rest and in transit must be evidenced.
5. Sub-processors must be listed and approved; unreported sub-processors are a contractual breach.

## 4. Data processing terms

Where personal data is involved, Legal_Data_Privacy_GDPR_Compliance requires a Data Processing Agreement. The DPA must cover purpose limitation, breach notification within 72 hours, deletion on termination and audit rights. Vendors that cannot accept the standard terms are escalated to Legal.

## 5. Ongoing monitoring

1. Confidential and Restricted vendors are reassessed annually.
2. A vendor security incident must be reported to Meridian within 72 hours under the DPA.
3. Access granted to vendor staff is reviewed quarterly with the vendor's named contacts.
4. Vendors that fail two consecutive reassessments are placed on a remediation plan and may be terminated by the business owner.

## 6. Exceptions

An exception requires the CTO's written approval, a compensating control and an expiry date no later than 90 days. Exceptions are reported to the security committee monthly.

## 7. Related documents

- IT_Access_Control_Standard for vendor accounts.
- Legal_Contract_Review_Process

# Revenue Recognition Policy

## 1. Principle

Revenue is recognised when control of the promised service passes to the customer, in the amount the company expects to be entitled to. Meridian applies the five-step model: identify the contract, identify the performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate the price to the obligations, and recognise revenue as each obligation is satisfied.

## 2. Contract identification

A contract exists when it is approved, the rights and payment terms are identifiable, it has commercial substance, and collection is probable. Orders below INR 1,00,000 with a standard online acceptance are treated as contracts on acceptance. Deals with non-standard terms require Legal_Contract_Review_Process before revenue can be scheduled.

## 3. Performance obligations

1. Subscription access is a series of distinct daily services recognised over the contract term.
2. Implementation services are a separate obligation when the customer can benefit from them independently; otherwise they are combined with the subscription.
3. Training is a separate obligation recognised when delivered.
4. Hardware resold with software is recognised on delivery.

## 4. Transaction price

1. The transaction price includes fixed fees and variable consideration that is probable and estimable.
2. Discounts are allocated proportionally across obligations unless the contract evidences a standalone price for one obligation.
3. Rebates and service credits are estimated and constrained until the uncertainty resolves.
4. Significant financing components are adjusted where payment terms exceed 12 months.

## 5. Milestone and deferred revenue

1. Annual prepayments are recorded as deferred revenue and released monthly over the term.
2. Milestone billing on implementation is recognised against delivery of the milestone, not against the invoice date.
3. Where a milestone is invoiced before delivery, the balance sits in deferred revenue.
4. Where delivery precedes invoicing, an unbilled receivable is recorded.

## 6. Contract modifications

A modification is treated as a separate contract if it adds distinct services priced at standalone selling price. Otherwise the remaining consideration is reallocated over the remaining obligations. Modifications must be documented by the deal desk and approved by the Controller.

## 1. Definition

A purchase is capital expenditure when it costs more than INR 10,00,000 and provides benefit for more than 12 months. Below that threshold the purchase is expensed in the quarter it is incurred, even if it is hardware. Software subscriptions are expensed unless the contract grants a perpetual licence, in which case the licence fee is capitalised and the support element is expensed.

## 2. Approval

1. Capex requires a business case covering the problem, the options considered, the total cost of ownership, the payback period and the risk of not proceeding.
2. A payback period longer than 24 months requires the CFO's approval; longer than 36 months requires board approval.
3. Every capex request must name the budget line in Finance_Quarterly_Budget_Allocation.
4. Capex above INR 50,00,000 is reviewed by the investment committee, which meets monthly.

## 3. Capitalisation and depreciation

| Asset class | Useful life | Method |
|---|---|---|
| Computer hardware | 3 years | Straight line |
| Network equipment | 5 years | Straight line |
| Furniture and fixtures | 7 years | Straight line |
| Perpetual software licences | 3 years | Straight line |
| Leasehold improvements | Shorter of lease or 5 years | Straight line |

Depreciation starts in the month the asset is available for use, not the month it is paid for. Assets not yet in use are held as capital work in progress and reviewed each quarter.

## 4. Impairment

Assets are reviewed for impairment annually or when there is an indicator such as a product being discontinued. An impairment loss is recognised in the quarter it is identified and reported to the CFO.

## 5. Disposal

1. Disposal requires the asset owner's request and Finance approval.
2. Proceeds are recorded against the asset's net book value; any gain or loss is recognised in the income statement.
3. Data-bearing assets must be wiped under IT_Data_Classification_Standard before disposal, with a certificate retained.
4. Disposals above INR 5,00,000 are reported to the audit committee.

## 6. Leases

Leases longer than 12 months are recognised on the balance sheet in line with the applicable accounting standard. The facilities team maintains the lease register and provides it to Finance quarterly.

# Vendor Payment Terms

## 1. Default terms

1. The default payment term for vendor invoices is Net 45 from the invoice date.
2. The invoice date is the date the invoice is issued, not the date it is received.
3. Payment runs happen twice a month, on the 10th and the 25th. An invoice falling due between runs is paid on the next run.
4. Vendors must quote a purchase order number on every invoice; invoices without one are returned unpaid.

## 2. Early payment discount

1. Where a vendor offers a 2% discount for payment within 10 days, Accounts Payable takes the discount if the cash position allows.
2. The discount is calculated on the invoice value excluding taxes.
3. Discounts are recorded as a separate line in the vendor ledger, not netted against the payable.
4. Vendors offering a discount for payment within 5 days are reviewed by the treasury team before acceptance.

## 3. Invoice validation

1. A three-way match is required: purchase order, goods receipt and invoice.
2. Mismatches are resolved with the business owner within 5 working days.
3. Invoices above INR 10,00,000 require a second Finance review.
4. Duplicate invoices are flagged by the vendor ledger and are never paid twice.

## 4. Late payment

1. Interest is payable on late invoices at 1% per month where the delay exceeds 30 days beyond the agreed term.
2. Interest is not payable where the delay is caused by a missing purchase order or a disputed invoice.
3. Persistent late payment is reported to the CFO monthly.

## 5. Small invoices

Invoices below INR 5,00,000 are settled on Net 30 rather than Net 45. This exception exists to reduce the administrative cost of low-value payables and does not require a contract amendment. Where a contract states Net 45 for a vendor whose invoices are consistently below the threshold, Accounts Payable applies Net 30 and records the deviation in the vendor file. Business owners should expect the shorter term when planning cash.

## 6. Foreign currency

Foreign currency invoices are paid in the invoice currency. The exchange rate is the bank rate on the payment date. Vendors may not require payment in a currency other than the contract currency.

# Revenue Recognition Policy

## 1. Principle

Revenue is recognised when control of the promised service passes to the customer, in the amount the company expects to be entitled to. Meridian applies the five-step model: identify the contract, identify the performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate the price to the obligations, and recognise revenue as each obligation is satisfied.

## 2. Contract identification

A contract exists when it is approved, the rights and payment terms are identifiable, it has commercial substance, and collection is probable. Orders below INR 1,00,000 with a standard online acceptance are treated as contracts on acceptance. Deals with non-standard terms require Legal_Contract_Review_Process before revenue can be scheduled.

## 3. Performance obligations

1. Subscription access is a series of distinct daily services recognised over the contract term.
2. Implementation services are a separate obligation when the customer can benefit from them independently; otherwise they are combined with the subscription.
3. Training is a separate obligation recognised when delivered.
4. Hardware resold with software is recognised on delivery.

## 4. Transaction price

1. The transaction price includes fixed fees and variable consideration that is probable and estimable.
2. Discounts are allocated proportionally across obligations unless the contract evidences a standalone price for one obligation.
3. Rebates and service credits are estimated and constrained until the uncertainty resolves.
4. Significant financing components are adjusted where payment terms exceed 12 months.

## 5. Milestone and deferred revenue

1. Annual prepayments are recorded as deferred revenue and released monthly over the term.
2. Milestone billing on implementation is recognised against delivery of the milestone, not against the invoice date.
3. Where a milestone is invoiced before delivery, the balance sits in deferred revenue.
4. Where delivery precedes invoicing, an unbilled receivable is recorded.

## 6. Contract modifications

A modification is treated as a separate contract if it adds distinct services priced at standalone selling price. Otherwise the remaining consideration is reallocated over the remaining obligations. Modifications must be documented by the deal desk and approved by the Controller.

## 1. Scope

This policy covers business travel and reimbursable expenses for all employees and contractors travelling on Meridian business. It sets the approval path, the limits and the evidence required. Expenses outside the limits are not reimbursed unless an exception is approved before the spend.

## 2. Approval before booking

1. All domestic travel requires manager approval before booking.
2. International travel requires manager and department head approval.
3. Travel to a country where Meridian has no entity also requires Legal review for immigration and tax.
4. Bookings made without approval are reimbursed only at the discretion of the Finance business partner.
5. Travel must be booked through the corporate travel tool; direct bookings are reimbursed only when the tool cannot serve the route.

1. Economy class for flights under six hours.
2. Premium economy for flights of six hours or more.

# Procurement Approval Matrix

## 1. Purpose

This matrix defines who may approve a purchase and what evidence is required at each value. It applies to goods and services bought from third parties, including software subscriptions, hardware, professional services and events. It does not apply to travel, which follows Finance_Travel_And_Expense_Policy, or to employee expenses, which follow Finance_Expense_Card_Policy.

## 2. Approval thresholds

| Purchase value (INR) | Approver | Evidence required |
|---|---|---|
| 0 to 50,000 | Manager | Quote or price confirmation |
| 50,001 to 5,00,000 | Director | Two quotes, business justification |

## 1. Background

Meridian moved to a hybrid model in 2022. Between 2022 and 2025 the expectation was set locally by each department, which produced inconsistent attendance and made desk planning unreliable. This mandate replaces departmental guidance with a single company-wide minimum. It supersedes all previous versions in full; where a team charter conflicts with this document, this document governs.

3. Employees whose role is designated on-site-only must attend 5 days per week.
4. Attendance is measured by badge-in events, not by calendar blocks. Two badge-ins on the same day count as one day.
5. A week containing a public holiday is pro-rated: three on-site days are required in a four-day week.

## 3. Anchor days

Tuesday and Thursday are company anchor days. Every team must have at least 80% attendance on anchor days. Team offsites, customer visits and approved travel count as attendance. Anchor days may be moved for a whole team by the department head with two weeks' notice, but not more than twice per quarter.

# Annual Leave and Carry-Forward Policy

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how paid annual leave is earned, requested, approved and carried forward at Meridian Technologies. It applies to all permanent employees in India, Singapore and the United Kingdom who are on payroll as of 1 January 2026. Contractors, interns and staff on fixed-term agreements shorter than six months are covered by their engagement letter instead and must not use the leave balances described here. Where a local statutory entitlement exceeds the entitlement in this policy, the statutory minimum applies and the difference is reported by People Operations in the quarterly compliance pack.

## 2. Entitlement

1. Full-time employees accrue 24 days of paid annual leave per calendar year.
2. Accrual is monthly and pro-rated from the date of joining. An employee joining on the 15th of a month accrues half of that month's entitlement.
3. Part-time employees accrue on a pro-rata basis using contracted hours divided by 40.
4. Employees on probation accrue leave from their first day but may not take more than five days until probation is confirmed.
5. Unused annual leave may be carried forward into the following calendar year up to a maximum of 12 days.
6. Carried-forward days must be used by 31 March of the year into which they were carried. Any balance remaining after 31 March is forfeited without payment in lieu.

Carry-forward is calculated by the payroll system on 31 December and appears on the January payslip. 5. During a declared incident (Sev-1 or Sev-2), approved leave for on-call staff may be cancelled by the incident commander. Cancelled days are restored in full and are exempt from the carry-forward cap for that year.

# Capital Expenditure Policy

## 1. Definition

A purchase is capital expenditure when it costs more than INR 10,00,000 and provides benefit for more than 12 months. Below that threshold the purchase is expensed in the quarter it is incurred, even if it is hardware. Software subscriptions are expensed unless the contract grants a perpetual licence, in which case the licence fee is capitalised and the support element is expensed.

## 2. Approval

1. Capex requires a business case covering the problem, the options considered, the total cost of ownership, the payback period and the risk of not proceeding.
2. A payback period longer than 24 months requires the CFO's approval; longer than 36 months requires board approval.
3. Every capex request must name the budget line in Finance_Quarterly_Budget_Allocation.
4. Capex above INR 50,00,000 is reviewed by the investment committee, which meets monthly.

## 3. Capitalisation and depreciation

| Asset class | Useful life | Method |
|---|---|---|
| Computer hardware | 3 years | Straight line |
| Network equipment | 5 years | Straight line |
| Furniture and fixtures | 7 years | Straight line |
| Perpetual software licences | 3 years | Straight line |
| Leasehold improvements | Shorter of lease or 5 years | Straight line |

Depreciation starts in the month the asset is available for use, not the month it is paid for. Assets not yet in use are held as capital work in progress and reviewed each quarter.

## 4. Impairment

Assets are reviewed for impairment annually or when there is an indicator such as a product being discontinued. An impairment loss is recognised in the quarter it is identified and reported to the CFO.

## 5. Disposal

1. Disposal requires the asset owner's request and Finance approval.
2. Proceeds are recorded against the asset's net book value; any gain or loss is recognised in the income statement.

# Incident Response Runbook

## 1. Severity definitions

1. **Sev-1** — customer-facing outage or data loss affecting more than 20% of customers, or any confirmed security breach.
2. **Sev-2** — degraded service affecting a material subset of customers, or an internal system blocking a revenue process.
3. **Sev-3** — limited impact with a workaround.
4. **Sev-4** — cosmetic or single-user issue.

Severity is declared by the on-call engineer and may be raised by the incident commander at any time. Downgrading a Sev-1 requires the incident commander and the engineering director.

## 2. Response windows

| Step | Sev-1 | Sev-2 |
|---|---|---|
| Acknowledge page | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Open incident channel | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Status page update | 30 minutes | 2 hours |
| Customer communication | 1 hour | 4 hours |

Missing an acknowledgement window is tracked as a reliability metric, not a disciplinary matter, unless it is repeated.

## 3. Roles

The incident commander owns the incident and does not debug. The communications lead writes status updates. The subject-matter engineers investigate. The scribe keeps the timeline. For a Sev-1, the incident commander is the on-call engineering manager; for a Sev-2 it may be the on-call engineer.

## 4. Process

2. Open the bridge. For a Sev-1, the bridge must open within 15 minutes of declaration; see Operations_Sev_Incident_Escalation for the current runbook version.
3. Assign the four roles.
4. Mitigate first, diagnose second. Roll back if the change is the suspected cause.
5. Update the status page at the intervals in Section 2.

# Change Management Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy controls how changes reach production so that reliability is not traded for speed. It applies to application deploys, infrastructure changes, database migrations, configuration changes and third-party integrations. Documentation-only changes and changes made entirely inside a feature-flagged path that is off in production are exempt.

## 2. Change types

1. **Standard** — pre-approved, low-risk changes with a documented runbook, such as a routine dependency patch or a dashboard update.
2. **Normal** — any change that is not standard or emergency; requires review and a change record.
3. **Emergency** — a change needed to resolve an active Sev-1 or Sev-2. Emergency changes may proceed with verbal approval from the incident commander and are recorded retrospectively within one business day.

## 3. Normal change process

1. Open a change record describing the change, the systems affected, the rollback plan and the monitoring plan.
2. Obtain code review from at least one engineer who is not the author.
3. Obtain approval from the system owner. Changes touching payment flows also require Finance sign-off.
4. Submit to the Change Advisory Board (CAB) at least 5 business days before the planned deployment window.
5. Deploy in the approved window and watch the dashboards for 30 minutes.
6. Close the change record with the observed outcome.

The CAB meets every Tuesday at 15:00 IST. Changes submitted after the Monday 12:00 cut-off are considered the following week. A change rejected by the CAB may be re-submitted once with the requested amendments.

## 4. Deployment windows

Production deploys are permitted Monday to Thursday, 10:00 to 17:00 IST. Friday deploys require the engineering director's approval. No production changes are made during the end-of-quarter freeze, from the 25th of the last month of each quarter until the second working day of the next quarter, except for emergency changes and security patches.

## 5. Rollback

Every normal change must have a tested rollback plan. Database migrations must be backward compatible for at least one release so the application can roll back without restoring data. A change without a rollback plan is rejected by the CAB.

2. If the change is implicated in an incident, roll back first and investigate afterwards.

# Vendor Security Review

## 1. When a review is required

Any third party that will store, process or access Meridian data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. This includes SaaS tools, contractors with system access, managed services and data processors. A review is not required for vendors that receive only Public information, but the classification must be recorded.

## 2. Process and timelines

1. The business owner submits the vendor request with the intended data classification and integration scope.
2. Security Engineering sends the standard questionnaire within 2 working days.
3. The vendor returns the questionnaire and evidence. The review concludes within 30 days of receiving complete evidence.
4. Reviews requiring a penetration test summary or a Data Processing Agreement take up to 45 days.
5. Contracts must not be signed before the review is recorded as passed.

## 3. Evidence requirements

1. SOC 2 Type II is required for any vendor processing Confidential or Restricted data. A SOC 2 Type I is accepted only with a remediation plan and a follow-up date.
2. ISO 27001 certification is accepted in place of SOC 2 where the scope covers the service in question.
3. Vendors without either certification require a documented compensating review by Security Engineering and approval from the CTO.
4. Encryption at rest and in transit must be evidenced.
5. Sub-processors must be listed and approved; unreported sub-processors are a contractual breach.

## 4. Data processing terms

Where personal data is involved, Legal_Data_Privacy_GDPR_Compliance requires a Data Processing Agreement. The DPA must cover purpose limitation, breach notification within 72 hours, deletion on termination and audit rights. Vendors that cannot accept the standard terms are escalated to Legal.

## 5. Ongoing monitoring

1. Confidential and Restricted vendors are reassessed annually.
2. A vendor security incident must be reported to Meridian within 72 hours under the DPA.
3. Access granted to vendor staff is reviewed quarterly with the vendor's named contacts.
4. Vendors that fail two consecutive reassessments are placed on a remediation plan and may be terminated by the business owner.

## 6. Exceptions

An exception requires the CTO's written approval, a compensating control and an expiry date no later than 90 days. Exceptions are reported to the security committee monthly.

## 7. Related documents

- IT_Access_Control_Standard for vendor accounts.
- Legal_Contract_Review_Process

# Access Control Standard

## 1. Scope

This standard defines how identities are created, authenticated, authorised and removed across Meridian systems. It applies to employees, contractors, service accounts and third-party integrations. Where a system cannot meet this standard, the exception is documented and approved by the security team with a remediation date.

## 2. Authentication

1. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for every system that holds Internal, Confidential or Restricted data.
2. Passwords must be at least 14 characters and are checked against a breach corpus at set time.
3. Shared accounts are prohibited. Service accounts must be owned by a named team and rotated every 90 days.
4. Session lifetime is 12 hours for web applications and 8 hours for administrative consoles.
5. SSH access requires a hardware key or a short-lived certificate; password authentication is disabled.

## 3. Authorisation

1. Access follows least privilege: the minimum needed to do the job, granted per role.
2. Role definitions are owned by the system owner and reviewed quarterly.
3. Privileged access — production write, cloud administration, payment systems — is granted for a maximum of 90 days and requires a second approver.
4. Access to customer data requires the data owner's approval and is logged.
5. A manager's approval is required for any new role assignment and is recorded in the access system.

## 4. Reviews

1. Every quarter, managers review the access of their direct reports and confirm or revoke.
2. Reviews are due within 10 working days of the request; overdue reviews escalate to the department head.
3. Dormant accounts with no login for 60 days are disabled automatically.
4. Contractor accounts expire on the engagement end date without exception.

## 5. Joiner, mover, leaver

Joining access is provisioned from the HR record on day one (see HR_Employee_Onboarding_Guide). A role change triggers a re-review of all access within five working days.
